topic: Argentine tango dance compared to mindfulness meditation and a waiting-list control: a randomised trial for treating depression

sources.title: Argentine tango dance compared to mindfulness meditation and a waiting-list control: a randomised trial for treating depression
sources.authors: Pinniger R, Brown RF, Thorsteinsson EB, McKinley P.

findings.finding: Tango dancing is an effective intervention for reducing depression symptoms in individuals.
findings.quote: Depression levels were significantly reduced in the tango (effect size d=0.50, p=.010), and meditation groups (effect size d=0.54, p=.025), relative to waiting-list controls.

findings.finding: Tango classes specifically help in lowering stress levels for participants.
findings.quote: Stress levels were significantly reduced only in the tango group (effect size d=0.45, p=.022).

findings.finding: Engagement in tango dance practice is linked to higher levels of mindfulness.
findings.quote: Attending tango classes was a significant predictor for the increased levels of mindfulness R(2)=.10, adjusted R(2)=.07, F (2,59)=3.42, p=.039.

principle: Participating in structured dance classes like Argentine tango can significantly reduce symptoms of depression and stress while promoting mindfulness.
for_the_teacher: Frame the dance practice as a tool for stress reduction and mindfulness to encourage consistent participation.
Structure lessons to include moments of focused attention to help learners cultivate mindfulness while they move.
when_it_does_not_apply: The study focused on individuals with self-declared depression and may not generalize to all populations; the intervention was a six-week program.
